reason: E2 shows a Volta potential difference between L12 (FCC) and B2 phases, supporting the electrochemical heterogeneity premise. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that wear removes the oxide layer, that this removal activates microgalvanic coupling, or that such coupling accelerates pitting and wear under simultaneous wear-corrosion conditions. E1 only addresses static corrosion after heat treatment, not the dynamic wear-corrosion interaction central to the hypothesis.
premises: Wear removes the protective oxide layer on eutectic HEAs
FCC and B2 phases in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 have different electrochemical potentials
Exposed phase boundaries with potential differences form microgalvanic cells
Microgalvanic coupling accelerates localized corrosion (pitting) at interfaces
Accelerated pitting exacerbates wear, leading to deeper wear tracks
